text:
Port your own Nintendo Switch games to Android, natively: the game's own arm64 code runs on the device, with the Switch's system services stood in for by a host and NVN graphics replayed on Vulkan. Pick the game's folder, click Port , and get an APK plus the game's data, installed on your device if you like. Bring your own game files and keys; nothing from any game is in this repository.

This is the Android port of nxnative, which does the same on iPhone and iPad. Supported games: Games.

 Games

These games play on Android. Click a game for its page: its status, the game update and the nx2android version it was tested with, the frame rate, the devices it was tested on, the options to set and its known quirks. The device's GPU must read BC-compressed textures (Adreno, Xclipse; not Mali or PowerVR).

A game's page names the latest nx2android version the game was tested on ( v0.1.3 ). Older games are not tested again for each release: if a later version breaks one, a patch release fixes it. A version newer than the latest release is the next release, and the game needs the development checkout until it ships.

A game that is not in this list is not supported yet. The games we look at next, and the ones done: docs/PORT CHECKLIST.md.

 For players: port a game without programming

1. Download nx2android- -windows-x64.zip (Windows), nx2android- -macos-arm64.zip (Mac with Apple silicon), nx2android- -linux-x64.zip (Linux on a PC) or nx2android- -linux-arm64.zip (Linux on ARM) from Releases, unzip it and start nx2android (on a Mac, see packaging/INSTALL.md first). On Linux you can take the nx2android- -linux-x64.AppImage or -linux-arm64.AppImage instead: make it executable and start it.
2. Setup tab: click Download missing tools (the Android NDK, the .NET SDK and platform-tools, about 1 GB, from Google and Microsoft), then set your prod.keys . Every line turns green.
3. Port tab: choose the folder with the game's NSP, XCI, NSZ or XCZ files (base game, update, DLC) and click Port .
4. Tick Install on the device when done with the device plugged in and USB debugging on, or copy the APK and the data folder yourself.

Pokémon Legends: Arceus and Pokémon Legends: Z-A need the device during the port, even without Install on the device when done : their shaders are in Oodle-compressed archives, which the port decodes with the game's own decoder on the device. Have platform-tools (adb) from step 2, and plug in the device with USB debugging on before you click Port .

A game played by touch: tick Touch game on the Port tab ( --touch ). The on-screen gamepad then starts hidden and every touch but one on the menu button goes to the game; the pause menu shows the gamepad again.

Chinese or Korean text drawn as ??? : choose a TrueType font with those characters as System font on the Port tab ( --shared-font , a single .ttf , not a .ttc ). It goes in the data pack; the tool ships none. The font needs Latin letters too, and a static one is safest: Super Mario Odyssey crashed at start with a phone's Hangul-only variable font. devtools/make shared font.py merges fonts you have into one such font, for example your Android phone's own Roboto and Korean font with --adb ( python devtools/make shared font.py --adb -o korean.ttf ). It is not in the zip: run it from a clone of this repository, with Python 3.11 or later and requirements.txt installed. The tool's own text entry panel shows those characters in its title and the game's initial text, but its keyboard types only ASCII.
